comments.content: The free condition is inverted/broken: `span->txt == NULL && span->static_flag` only ever calls `lv_free(NULL)` (a no-op), so a previously owned text buffer is never released. Every call that overwrites an existing dynamically allocated span text leaks the old buffer (e.g. `lv_spangroup_bind_span_text` re-formatting the same span on every subject change grows memory without bound). The same bug is duplicated in `lv_spangroup_set_span_text_fmt`. The intended guard is to free only the owned (non-static) text, consistent with `lv_span_set_text_static`/`lv_spangroup_delete_span`.

`va_end(args)` is skipped on the `text == NULL` early-return path (also in `lv_spangroup_set_span_text_fmt`). Pairing every `va_start` with `va_end` is required; leaving it out on an error path is undefined behavior. Move `va_end` before the NULL check (as `lv_label_set_text_fmt` does) so all exits release the va_list.

`lv_spangroup_set_span_text_fmt` duplicates the whole body of `lv_span_set_text_fmt` (va_list handling, buffer ownership, assignment) and only adds `lv_spangroup_refresh`. This duplicates the ownership logic (and the bug above) in two places. Consider extracting a shared static helper taking a `va_list` (e.g. `span_set_text_vfmt(span, fmt, args)`), or have both public functions funnel through one implementation, so fixes only have to be made once.
